title: Expert Evaluation of LLM's Open-Ended Legal Reasoning on the Japanese Bar Exam Writing Task

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 ('The o3 model does not provide explicit sampling parameters for users. For the reasoning effort, we used a default of medium. Unless otherwise stated, no explicit maximum output token limit was imposed'); max_tokens is our own generous allowance

task.subset_rule: the 21 essay questions of the Japanese bar exam 2021-2023 (7 compulsory subjects per year), zero-shot setting
task.approximation: Only the ZS setting is the claimed cell; FS and FS+Law add in-context examples from the 2018 and 2019 exams and statutory references from the authors' dataset.

items.source: the official published Japanese bar exam questions for 2021-2023 (Ministry of Justice); the authors' processed dataset, including the statutory references used in FS+Law, is not released
items.config_or_split: seven compulsory subjects (Constitution, Civil Code, Penal Code, administrative law, Code of Civil Procedure, Code of Criminal Procedure, commercial law) for each of 2021, 2022, 2023

prompt.system: not printed: Sec. 4.1 says that 'for all models, system prompts assign the role of a Japanese legal expert and require that outputs be based on Japanese law and written in a casual form (non-polite form)'
prompt.user_template: the exam question verbatim, preceded by the temporal-scope instruction quoted in Sec. 4.1: 'Answer based on laws and regulations in force as of [the date of the examination]'

placeholders.question: the official exam question text
placeholders.date: the date of that year's examination

prompt.few_shot: none in the ZS setting (FS uses 2018 and 2019 questions with sample answers)
prompt.verbatim: partial: one instruction sentence is quoted, the system prompt is only described, and the Japanese wording of both is not printed

output.postprocess: the answer is a full written bar-exam essay in Japanese

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: average expert score on a 0-100 scale over the 21 questions, graded by seven legal-faculty evaluators against the official grading criteria (the paper also reports categorical grades: excellent / good / adequate / poor)
metric.original_location: Table 1, row 'o3 ZS', column Avg. (per-subject scores 18.7 / 31.3 / 51.3 / 34.7 / 10.7 / 40.7 / 21.3; categorical grades 0 excellent, 3 good, 0 adequate, 18 poor)

open_points: The metric is a human expert score: reproducing the number needs seven equivalent Japanese legal-faculty graders, not API calls. No LLM judge is defined in the paper, so no judge stage can stand in for it.
The system prompt and the Japanese wording of the instruction are not printed, only described.
The 21 exam questions are public documents but are not released as a machine-readable dataset by the authors; they would have to be transcribed from the Ministry of Justice exam papers.
notes: The o3 FS (29.4) and FS+Law (30.5) rows are the same questions with in-context examples and statutes. GPT-4o in this paper is gpt-4o-2024-11-20 and Claude 3 Opus is claude-3-opus-20240229, so o3-2025-04-16 is the live-listed snapshot. The hallucination analysis (Tables 2-3) is a second human annotation layer on the same outputs.
